title: Gulf Coast drivers warned about summer tire dangers - NewsBreak
text: MOBILE COUNTY, Ala. ( WKRG ) — Summers on the Gulf Coast don’t just put you at risk of overheating, but also your vehicle. Technicians at Fausak in Saraland know that better than anyone. During the hot summer months, they’re especially busy helping customers with air conditioning repairs and fixing or replacing tires. “As the heat goes up, so does the temperature inside the tire,” Fausak District Manager Donald Herrera said. “For about every 10 pounds, you’re going to see an extra PSI of one pound in the tire, so you’re going to see that if you’re not careful, that tire is going to inflate, overinflate, and that’s when you’re going to have blowouts.” Herrera says most vehicles will let you know when your tire pressure is low, though it’s a different story when it’s high. “When the temperatures are rising, there [are] very few that [are] going to give you a high temperature bump,” Herrera explained. “So it’s a good idea to check your tire pressure about once a month, making sure that they stay inflated properly.” Doing all you can to prevent replacing a tire is advisable, or it could cost you. “A tire could run anywhere from $150 to $300, $400 a piece. It just depends on what you want to put into your vehicle,” Herrera said. Another thing drivers may not know, the scorching sun can also cause tires to dry rot. “You’ll see some cracking around the edges, sidewall damage, stuff like that,” Herrera said. “You can come in; either might need an alignment, there might be a rotation, you might need to get a new set of tires if they’re dry rotted and they’ve been on there for a while.” To keep yourself and your wallet from cracking under the Gulf Coast sun, Herrera recommends rotating your tires and routine maintenance to help with their lifespan and wear. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WKRG News 5.
